activities.label: Product rule model
activities.title: Product rule overview
activities.body: Read the model, then move on to your own explanation.

essentialIdeas: The product rule differentiates a product of two functions by combining the derivative of the first factor times the second factor, plus the first factor times the derivative of y.

activities.label: Explain product rule
activities.title: Product rule from memory
activities.body: In one or two sentences, explain the rule in your own words.
activities.concept: Product rule
activities.correctAnswer: When differentiating a product of two functions, take the derivative of the first times the second, then add the first times the derivative of the second.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names both terms in the sum and makes clear that a product is not differentiated by multiplying the derivatives together.

activities.label: Repair product rule
activities.title: Fix the product rule step
activities.body: Correct the rule after comparing your explanation with the model.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Differentiating a product means multiplying the derivatives of both factors.
activities.concept: Product rule
activities.correctAnswer: The derivative of a product is first derivative times second, plus first times second derivative.
activities.feedback: That repair keeps the two-term structure. The common mistake is to use a product of derivatives instead of a sum of two terms.

activities.label: Chain rule model
activities.title: Chain rule overview
activities.body: Read the model, then move on to your own explanation.

essentialIdeas: The chain rule differentiates a composite function by taking the derivative of the outer function and multiplying by the derivative of the inner function.

activities.label: Explain chain rule
activities.title: Chain rule from memory
activities.body: In one or two sentences, explain the rule in your own words.
activities.concept: Chain rule
activities.correctAnswer: For a composite function, differentiate the outside first and then multiply by the derivative of the inside.
activities.feedback: A complete answer identifies both outer and inner parts and shows the multiply-by-inner-derivative step.

activities.label: Check chain rule recognition
activities.title: Choose the chain rule form
activities.body: Pick the expression that uses the chain rule correctly.
activities.concept: Chain rule
choices: Differentiate the outside function, then multiply by the derivative of the inside function.
Differentiate both parts and add them.
Multiply the two original functions, then differentiate the result.
Differentiate only the inside function and leave the outside unchanged.
activities.correctAnswer: Differentiate the outside function, then multiply by the derivative of the inside function.
activities.feedback: Chain rule means outer derivative times inner derivative. The other choices leave out the composition structure or use an unrelated operation.
